title: Normalizer quotients and rank-one root interfaces
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $T,G,H$ be $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme]. Use the multiplicative and additive group schemes and affine test schemes of [def-sc-gm-ga], closed and normal subgroup schemes of [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], smoothness [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connectedness [def-weil-connected-scheme], tori and largest subtori [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type], maximal tori and reductivity [def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology], affine algebraic groups and represented fppf quotients [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure], derived subgroups and derived-series solvability [def-sfb-semisimple-group-scheme], character tangent weight spaces [def-sfb-torus-character-tangent-weights], and Krull dimension [def-kun-dimension]. Define $X(T)=\operatorname{Hom}(T,\mathbf G_m)$ and $Y(T)=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf G_m,T)$. For an action $a$ of $T$ on $G$, use the already defined character weight space $\mathfrak g_\chi$; define its roots as the nontrivial characters whose weight space is nonzero. For $i:T\to G$, the restricted adjoint action map is $(t,g)\mapsto i(t)g i(t)^{-1}$. On any test scheme $A$, let $I_i(A)$ be the image subgroup of $T(A)\to G(A)$. Let $N_i$ be the subgroup of $G(F)$ of points whose image normalizes $I_i(A)$ for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$, and also normalizes the image on the terminal test scheme. Set $D_i=I_i(F)\cap N_i$ as a subgroup of $N_i$; it is normal, and set $W_i=N_i/D_i$. For a $\mathbf G_m(A)$-point $z$, let $\operatorname{val}(z)$ be its Laurent coordinate $t$ evaluated in $A$. Say $H$ has semisimple rank one if it has a largest smooth connected solvable closed normal subgroup $r:R\to H$, with $R$ affine of finite type, and a represented fppf quotient $q:H\to Q$ with $Q$ affine of finite type, such that $Q$ has a maximal torus and every maximal torus of $Q$ has Krull dimension one. A morphism $v:\operatorname{SL}_2\to H$ is expressed equivalently as homomorphisms $v_A:\{g\in M_2(A):\det g=1\}\to H(A)$ natural in every commutative $F$-algebra $A$. A closed subgroup $d:D\to H$ is its scheme-theoretic image if it contains $v_A(\operatorname{SL}_2(A))$ for every $A$ and factors through every other closed subgroup with this property.
